newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks zoom in on record at close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks zoom in on record at close.

text.p: The Australian stock market, inspired by record highs on Wall Street, closed on Monday within striking distance of the record high of 2350.1 reached on February 3, 1994 despite a holiday in Sydney.
The All Ordinaries index closed 24.3 points or 1.05 percent higher at 2339.8, just off its intra-day high of 2341.1, its highest level this year.
Brokers said the All Ordinaries index could hit its record high on Tuesday if New York kept up its record run and there was no large drop in metal prices overnight.
"It has been a good performance given that there is not much happening locally today," said Helen Michael, a broker at Melbourne brokerage Peake Lands Kirwan.
There were public holidays in New South Wales, South Australia and in the Australian Capial Territory on Monday.
"I think it will test the record, but as soon as it does the profit-takers will come in and sell it down again," Michael said.
The market pepped up in the afternoon after drifting at midday to hit its highest close this year.

Stocks rose across the board. Market heavyweights BHP, CRA and News Corp led the way among the blue-chips. CRA made up about 20 percent of the share trade value on Monday, with A$100 million (US$79 million) of options-related trading.
News Corp shares were also heavily traded with the share price rising over four percent to its highest level since mid-July. News' preference shares were also higher.
Traders said the Federal Court approval of News' Super League competition was a short term boost for the shares.
Risers outnumbered falls by a ratio of three-to-two with about 30 percent of stocks traded being steady.
Transport, chemicals and the developers and contractors sectors were the only indices to go against the rising trend.
The Sydney Futures Exchange's (SFE) December share price index contract was up 22 at 2362 in after-hours computer trading, after being affected by a power outage.
The SFE floor was closed due to the holiday.
